title: What a CRO Agency Really Costs: Real Prices, Quotes and ROI Math
meta_title: CRO Agency Cost: Real Prices and What You Get
meta_description: What a CRO agency really costs: real prices for DIY, freelancers, in-house and agencies, how to compare quotes per test, and the 1,000-order traffic line.
teaser: Real CRO pricing from $0 to $35,000 a month, a formula to compare agency quotes, and the traffic you need before hiring anyone.
summary: A CRO agency costs anywhere from about $2,000 to $35,000 a month, but the extra money mostly buys testing velocity (how many tests ship each month), and how many tests you can actually run depends on your traffic. Compare quotes by price per test (monthly fee divided by tests shipped), and only hire a testing agency once your store does around 1,000 orders a month. Below that, get a CRO audit and fix the basics first.
key_takeaways: There are five ways to pay for CRO: do it yourself with a testing tool, hire a freelancer ($80 to $170 an hour), build an in-house team (about $300,000 a year in wages), hire an agency (mostly $2,000 to $15,000 a month), or sign a performance deal.
Divide each agency's monthly fee by the number of tests it actually ships to get a price per test, then compare quotes on that number.
Price per test is not price per learning: ask who analyzes the results, because spinning up variants is easy (especially with AI) but learning from them takes capacity.
Below roughly 1,000 orders a month, hold off on A/B testing. Get a CRO audit, apply the findings and fix the fundamentals first.
If you want performance pricing, ask for a fixed fee plus a smaller performance bonus instead of 20% of extra revenue, which gets expensive fast when a test wins big.

Before signing, ask when the first test will be live, make sure the senior person who will run your account is on the sales or onboarding call, and get any guarantee's calculation written into the agreement.
Run the ROI math on your own numbers: a 10% conversion lift on $300,000 a month is $30,000 extra per month, while on $50,000 a month an agency barely pays for itself.

sections.heading: How much does a CRO agency cost per month?

blocks.text: Our CRO program at Sparksmetrics starts at $2,800 a month. Other agencies easily charge $35,000 every single month. So what does that extra $32,000 actually buy you? Smarter people or better ideas? Not really.

What it buys is **higher testing velocity**: more tests shipped per month. That matters a lot when you optimize a store. But here is the catch: the agency you pick and how much you pay do not decide how many tests you can run. **Your traffic does.**

If you Google CRO agency pricing you get ranges like $5,000 to $15,000 or $3,000 to $7,000. They are all true and all useless, because they give you no indication of what you should pay. Often they are written by agencies that do not share their own prices. I run a CRO agency, so I will share real prices, including options that are much cheaper and much more expensive than us.

sections.heading: What are the 5 ways to pay for CRO?

blocks.text: There are five different ways to price a CRO effort. Here is the menu with real numbers.

items: **Do it yourself.** Shopify has a free built-in A/B testing tool called Rollouts. It is not as advanced as paid tools. Intelligems costs about $80 a month, and Convert or VWO easily go above $200 a month. Shopify's own tool is a very good way to start for free.

**Hire a freelancer.** A senior or mid-level CRO expert charges roughly $80 to $170 an hour. Great for a simple audit, not enough for a full CRO program, because there is rarely one person who is really good at strategy, design, development and analysis.

**Build it in-house.** A mid-level CRO expert working full-time in the US costs about $80,000 to $130,000 a year. One person cannot do it all, so you also need a designer and a developer. That is easily about **$300,000 a year in wage costs**.
**Hire an agency.** Most agencies charge about $2,000 to $15,000 a month, and some go beyond that.
**Performance deal.** You pay after you get results. It sounds good, but it often ends up way more expensive than any of the other options.

blocks.text: With the DIY route, remember that the tool is the cheap part. Deciding what to test, designing it, building it and reading the results without fooling yourself is the actual job, and it costs your time.

sections.heading: What sets a CRO agency's price, and how do you compare two quotes?

blocks.text: Most of you are comparing agencies. Why does one charge $2,000 while another charges $15,000 or $20,000? It comes down to **the number of tests per month**. Every test needs strategy, design, development, QA and, once it is live, analysis. That work repeats for every single test.

items: A $2,000 to $5,000 retainer roughly gets you three to four tests a month.
Above that, you can expect six to eight tests a month.

blocks.text: That number is your testing velocity, and the higher it is, the better your results. To compare two quotes, calculate the **price per test**: the monthly fee divided by the tests actually shipped. An agency running 10 tests for $10,000 costs $1,000 per test. One running two tests for $4,000 costs $2,000 per test.

There is an important caveat. You are comparing price per test, not **price per learning**. Input is not the same as output. Especially now with AI, you can spin up five versions of a whole site in an afternoon. You will have plenty of tests, but you will not learn much if nobody has the capacity to properly analyze the results that come in.

sections.heading: How much traffic do you need before hiring a CRO agency?

blocks.text: Testing only makes sense if your store has enough traffic to run tests and learn from them. An A/B test needs enough orders to tell you which variant actually won.

Take an imaginary store converting at 2%. To detect a 10% lift in conversion rate, you need about **160,000 sessions in the test**. That can take ages to accumulate, and if every test takes that long you cannot test many things.

items: 10 orders a day (about 500 sessions a day): one test takes about 11 months.
100 orders a day: one test takes about a month.
1,000 orders a month (about 30 a day): with a 20% uplift from your changes, you see statistically significant results in about 4 weeks.

blocks.text: So the line is **about 1,000 orders a month**. Below that, do not forget about conversion rate. Instead of testing, get a CRO audit done and improve your site with the findings. Hold off on testing and get the basics and fundamentals right first.

sections.heading: Is performance-based CRO pricing a good deal?

blocks.text: Say you have the traffic and a few quotes in. One option you will see is performance pricing. Generally the agency wants **20% of the additional revenue** created on your store. If one simple test makes $30,000, you pay them $6,000 for that one test.
It sounds fair, but there are three problems:

items: **It gets expensive when tests do well.** A big winner means a big bill.
**Incentives drift.** The agency may run simple, safe tests instead of the bigger swings that teach you what would lift performance much further.
**Attribution.** Agreeing on what revenue a test actually created can become an issue.

blocks.text: If you like this structure, I always suggest a **fixed fee plus a smaller performance bonus** on top. You stay aligned, and the agency still has enough incentive to push to the limits.

sections.heading: What do CRO agencies not tell you before you sign?

blocks.text: There are four things CRO agencies would probably rather not tell you.

items: **The first test can take three or four weeks.** The first month often goes to tracking, tools and research. In the interview, ask when the first test is expected to be live, and push that forward as much as you can.
**The person on the sales call may not run your account.** Make sure the senior CRO person you will work with daily is on the sales or onboarding call, so you know you are not handed to a junior.

**Most tests lose.** You pay to learn fast, not for winning tests. When we ran six tests for one client, four failed miserably and we killed them early. The two winners together made an additional $150,000 for that single client.

**Guarantees live in the fine print.** Read them, and get written into the agreement exactly how the benefit to your store is calculated. If an agency makes guarantees or promises, it should back them up during the engagement.

sections.heading: How do you calculate the ROI of a CRO agency?

blocks.text: The most important metric is plain ROI math: what does it cost and what do you get back?

Say your store does $300,000 a month at a 1.5% conversion rate. A 10% lift takes you to 1.65%, which is about **$30,000 in extra revenue every month**. Paying an agency $3,000 a month, that is a 10x return on your investment.
If your store does $50,000 a month, the same agency barely pays for itself. So honestly, the agency does not set whether the price is worth it. Your store does.

sections.heading: What does Sparksmetrics charge for CRO?

blocks.text: We have three packages: **$2,800, $4,800 and $6,800 a month**. The price depends on the size of your store. Bigger stores can run more tests, which brings more results. Every plan includes strategy, design, development, QA and analysis. The plan only changes the velocity, and on smaller stores we are simply capped by the traffic limit.

We are cheaper than American agencies because we work remotely from Europe, so our costs are much lower and we do not need $10,000+ monthly fees. Even our smallest plan runs at least four tests a month, about **$700 per test**.

We offer an ROI guarantee, meaning we always make more money for our clients than we charge, so we have skin in the game. If you have fewer than 1,000 orders a month, or you would be better off with someone else, that is fine. We are not for everybody.

To recap: CRO costs anywhere from free to $35,000 a month. Work with someone experienced, and make sure you deal directly with a senior person, not a junior. Then work out the possible ROI for your own Shopify store before you hire anyone.

faq.q: How much does a CRO agency cost per month?
faq.a: Most CRO agencies charge about $2,000 to $15,000 a month, and some charge up to $35,000. A $2,000 to $5,000 retainer typically gets you three to four tests a month, while higher fees get you six to eight. The extra money mostly buys testing velocity.

faq.q: How many orders do I need before running A/B tests on my Shopify store?
faq.a: The line is about 1,000 orders a month, roughly 30 a day. At that level, a change with a 20% uplift reaches statistical significance in about 4 weeks. Below it, tests take too long, so get a CRO audit and fix the fundamentals first.

faq.q: How do I compare two CRO agency quotes?
faq.a: Divide each monthly fee by the number of tests the agency actually ships to get a price per test. For example, 10 tests for $10,000 is $1,000 per test, while two tests for $4,000 is $2,000 per test. Also check who analyzes the results, because you want learnings, not just tests.

faq.q: Is performance-based CRO pricing worth it?
faq.a: Performance deals usually ask for 20% of the additional revenue, so a test that makes $30,000 costs you $6,000. That gets expensive when tests win big, can push the agency toward safe tests, and creates attribution issues. A fixed fee plus a smaller performance bonus keeps both sides aligned.

faq.q: Can I A/B test on Shopify for free?
faq.a: Yes. Shopify has a free built-in A/B testing tool called Rollouts. It is less advanced than paid tools like Intelligems (about $80 a month) or Convert and VWO (easily above $200 a month), but it is a good way to start. The hard part is deciding what to test, building it and reading the results correctly.

faq.q: How much does a CRO freelancer or in-house CRO team cost?
faq.a: A senior or mid-level CRO freelancer charges roughly $80 to $170 an hour, which works for an audit but rarely for a full program. A full-time mid-level CRO expert in the US costs about $80,000 to $130,000 a year. Add a designer and developer and you are at about $300,000 a year in wages.
